name: Lamina monopolar cell L1 (ON channel)
function: Sustained ON / brightness channel; main input from R1-R6 photoreceptors; feeds the ON motion pathway (L1 -> Mi1 -> T4).
references: Fischbach & Dittrich 1989; Borst 2018; Yang et al. 2016 (Cell)

name: Lamina monopolar cell L2 (OFF channel)
function: Transient OFF / contrast channel; feeds the OFF motion pathway (L2 -> Tm1/Tm2 -> T5).
references: Fischbach & Dittrich 1989; Borst 2018; Fu et al. 2020

name: Lamina monopolar cell L3 (sustained brightness)
function: Sustained luminance / contrast channel operating in darkness; modulates both ON and OFF pathways.

name: Transmedullary OFF-pathway cells (Tm1,Tm2,Tm3,Tm4,Tm9)
function: OFF-edge relay from lamina to lobula; Tm1/Tm2/Tm4/Tm9 provide the delayed and direct lines of the OFF motion detector.
references: Shinomiya et al. 2014; Takemura et al. 2017; Fu et al. 2020

name: Medulla intrinsic ON-pathway cells (Mi1,Mi4,Mi9,T2,T3)
function: ON-edge relay: Mi1 (direct) and Mi4/Mi9 (delayed) converge onto T4 dendrites.

name: T4a-d (ON direction-selective columnar neurons)
function: Direction-selective ON motion detectors; four subtypes (a,b,c,d) tile four directional preferences; principal input to lobula-plate tangential cells.
proposed_mapping: motion direction (ON edges), optic flow components

name: T5a-d (OFF direction-selective columnar neurons)
function: Direction-selective OFF motion detectors; four subtypes (a,b,c,d); converge with T4 onto the same tangential cells.
proposed_mapping: motion direction (OFF edges), optic flow components

name: Horizontal-system tangential cells (HSN,HSE,HSS)
function: Wide-field neurons integrating horizontal retinal large-field motion (optic flow); HSN/HSE/HSS are electrophysiologically characterized motion-vision neurons.

name: Vertical-system tangential cells (VS1-VS8)
function: Wide-field neurons integrating vertical retinal large-field motion (optic flow), each covering a distinct part of the visual field.

name: Lobula plate / lobula columnar type 2 (LPLC2)
function: Looming (expanding-edge) detector; encodes angular size/velocity of approaching objects; provides the dominant optic-lobe input to the giant fiber (DNp01) escape pathway.
references: von Reyn et al. 2017; Ache et al. 2019 (Curr Biol); Lopez et al. 2024

name: LPLC1 and LPLC4 (looming-family columnar neurons)
function: Looming-responsive columnar projection neurons of the lobula plate/lobula cluster; response properties distinct from LPLC2.
references: Wu et al. 2016 (eLife); Klapoetke et al. 2022

name: Lobula columnar LC4
function: Visual projection neuron contributing with LPLC2 most of the optic-lobe input to the giant fiber; required for normal timing of looming escape.
references: von Reyn et al. 2017; Williamson et al. 2018; Lopez et al. 2024

name: Lobula columnar LC16
function: Small-object / approaching-object detector; optogenetic activation induces backward walking hypothesised to be mediated by moonwalker descending neurons.
references: Sen et al. 2017 (Cell Rep); Wu et al. 2016

name: Lobula columnar LC17
function: Edge-motion sensitive visual projection neuron implicated in visual approach/looming-adjacent behaviours.
references: Wu et al. 2016; Klapoetke et al. 2022; preprint evidence 2026

name: Lobula columnar LC9
function: Visual projection neuron providing a major input to P9/DNp09 (forward-walking/turning command); part of the object-directed walking pathway.
references: Wu et al. 2016; Bidaye et al. 2020 (Neuron)

name: Medulla-to-tubercle neurons (MeTu)
function: Anterior visual pathway carrying (non-topographic and topographic) visual information via the bulb to the central complex (navigation/pol-ish-light cues); not a primary entry for game vision.
references: Omoto et al. 2017; Timaeus et al. 2020

name: Labellar sugar-sensing gustatory receptor neurons (tutorial set)
function: Sugar-taste sensory neurons; the tutorial stimulus set of the Shiu et al. model; establishes the precedent of sensory entry into the digital brain.
proposed_mapping: (legacy tutorial input; precedent for sensory entry)

name: Olfactory receptor neuron axons (class: olfactory)
function: Chemosensory entry into the antennal lobe; not used by the game (no olfactory display), registered for completeness.

name: Mechanosensory neurons (incl. Johnston's organ)
function: Mechanical vibration / sound entry (Johnston's organ); future optional entry point if game audio is ever mapped.
references: FlyWire v783 annotations; Kamikouchi et al. 2009
